title: 3PL Pricing Guide: Common Third-Party Logistics Costs
summary: Outsourcing fulfillment work to third-party logistics can help you scale ecommerce operations. Learn what 3PL services cost.
body_markdown:
3PL pricing is how third-party logistics (3PL) partners charge ecommerce brands to store, pick, pack, and transport customer orders.


Technical capabilities directly influence a company’s efficiency when it comes to fulfillment and pricing. According to the 2026[Annual Third-Party Logistics Study](https://www.3plstudy.com/ntt3pl/nttds_3pl.home) , 90% of shippers consider technology critical when selecting a 3PL partner, yet only 57% report being satisfied with their provider’s current capabilities. When software integrations lag, or inventory systems disconnect, businesses absorb the difference through manual tracking time and unexpected operational fees.


Learn how 3PL costs work across every stage, review the fee structures and pricing models facilities bill for, and uncover strategies to evaluate quotes and achieve cost savings.


## 3PL pricing: common fees and costs


- Setup and onboarding fees
- Inbound receiving and put-away
- Storage and warehouse fees
- Picking and packing
- Packaging materials
- Shipping costs and carrier rates
- Returns processing (reverse logistics)
- Potential hidden fees


Outsourced logistics pricing is divided into transaction fees, warehouse space costs, and freight rates. The actual cost of outsourcing[order fulfillment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/order-fulfillment) depends on your product dimensions,[inventory turnover](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-inventory-turnover) , and total order volume. Here’s how it all breaks down:


### Setup and onboarding fees


Onboarding covers the staff time needed to set up your account, configure catalog rules, and connect your sales channels to the warehouse management system.


Some 3PLs charge one-time setup or integration fees between $250 and $2,500, while others waive them. Costs cover the technical setup involved with mapping your[SKU](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-a-stock-keeping-unit) data, testing inventory sync frequencies, and routing orders automatically between your online store and warehouse floor.


Providers also charge standard setup fees to establish your account profile, build fulfillment workflows, and train warehouse staff on your product guidelines. Custom handling rules or strict compliance requirements increase the setup time and the resulting fee.


### Inbound receiving and put-away


Receiving covers offloading, counting, inspecting, and shelving product deliveries sent from your manufacturers to the fulfillment centers.


Warehouses bill for intake in two ways: by the hour ($35 to $55 per person-hour) or by the unit ($10 to $45 per pallet and 25¢ to $3.00 per carton). If shipments arrive without advance shipping notices, missing barcode labels, or stacked haphazardly on broken pallets, facilities charge extra sorting penalties. Palletize, label, and wrap cartons to spec at the factory before shipping them to the warehouse to lower the total labor required at the receiving dock.


### Storage and warehouse fees


Warehouse costs cover the space your products occupy across warehouse racks and bins. Warehouses bill for space based on volume rather than square footage.


Standard pallets cost between $10 and $40 each per month. Dedicated bins cost between $2 and $8 per location monthly. When handling irregular or fluctuating inventory volumes, facilities bill through cubic-foot pricing, charging between 45¢ and $1 per cubic foot every month.


Letting inventory sit unsold drains capital twice over; it ties up your inventory investment and racks up ongoing space fees. On *[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/harlem-candle-co-scent-of-success)* , Teri Johnson, founder of[Harlem Candle Co.](https://www.harlemcandleco.com/) , shared how producing luxury, slow-moving items like decorative glassware can trigger unexpected holding charges. “The longer you are sitting with a product like this in inventory at our warehouse, you’re paying bin fees every month. You’re paying storage fees,” she says.


To protect your margins, monitor your sales closely and clear out slow-moving items before holding charges outpace product profit.


**Storage Type** **Average** **Monthly Cost** **Best Suited For**


Pallet storage $15 to $40 per pallet Bulk overstock and fast-moving reserve inventory


Bin storage $2 to $8 per bin Small items, cosmetics, jewelry, and individual parts


Cubic foot 45¢ to $1 per cubic foot Irregular catalog shapes and varying stock volumes


### Picking and packing


Once an order syncs to the warehouse, staff locate each item and pack it into a shipping box. Pricing starts with an initial order handling fee that covers the first picked item, followed by an added fee for each additional SKU in the box.


On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/andrew-faris-pnl) , Andrew Faris, founder of[AJF Growth](https://ajfgrowth.com/) , broke down the baseline costs brands encounter, saying, “If I’m shipping through a 3PL, the cost of order fulfillment is usually $1 or $1.50.” He says there are also[pick-and-pack](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pick-and-pack-fulfillment) costs to consider, or how much it costs to find an item in storage and pack it up for shipment.


Base fulfillment fees cover the order ticket, the carton, and the first pick. The 3PL then adds secondary pick-and-pack fees (typically 20¢ to $1.50 per item) for each added item. Orders containing multiple items cost more to pick and pack than orders containing just one.


### Packaging materialst


Packaging costs cover the cardboard shipping box, paper or bubble wrap, tape, and packing slips.


Using a warehouse’s plain boxes and brown paper void-fill adds 10¢ to $2 per package. Supplying your own branded boxes, tissue paper, or stickers removes standard box fees, though warehouses often charge a handling fee to assemble complex, custom unboxing sets.


### Shipping costs and carrier rates


Outbound freight delivery accounts for the largest share of your total fulfillment costs. Carriers calculate[shipping costs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/common-shipping-questions) by comparing the shipment’s actual weight against its dimensional weight (DIM) and billing whichever number is higher.


Because 3PLs pool delivery volume across hundreds of retail clients, they negotiate discounted volume tier rates with major carriers like FedEx, UPS, DHL, and USPS, passing part of those savings along to merchants.


### Returns processing (reverse logistics)


[Reverse logistics](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/reverse-logistics) covers receiving a customer return, unboxing the parcel, inspecting the product, re-tagging or re-bagging it, and returning inventory to active shelves.


Standard returns processing costs between $2 and $10 per item, plus the price of the return shipping label. Products that arrive damaged or require steaming, cleaning, re-boxing, or scrapping incur added bench labor charges.


### Potential hidden fees


Audit contracts for administrative line items that inflate monthly invoices, such as:


-


**Account management fees.** Shared support tickets are usually included, but a dedicated account manager is an added fee to your monthly bill.


-


**Monthly minimums.** Most providers enforce monthly spending limits. For example, if your sales drop and fulfillment bills total $900, the warehouse charges you the full minimum balance.


-


**Peak season surcharges.** Between October and January, providers often apply surcharges across storage, receiving, and order handling to offset temporary holiday labor costs.


-


**Value-added services.** Facilities charge extra for special handling, including applying barcode stickers, tracking lots or serial numbers, managing hazardous materials, and preparing bulk business-to-business (B2B) retailer orders.

## Tips for finding the most efficient 3PL pricing


- Set clear contribution margin goals
- Dilute fixed fulfillment charges with product bundles
- Audit inventory holding times to avoid excess storage fees
- Standardize and minimize package dimensions
- Compare vetted logistics providers inside Shopify


Lowering your 3PL expenses requires careful product design and disciplined[contract management](https://www.shopify.com/blog/contract-management) . Use these strategies to keep your logistics spending in check:


### Set clear contribution margin goals


Before signing a 3PL contract, calculate your per-unit costs to confirm that your pricing can absorb fulfillment fees. DTC businesses track this through[contribution margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-contribution-margin) , which is calculated by taking your net sales price, subtracting the[cost of goods sold (COGS)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cost-of-goods-sold) , and then subtracting all direct logistics, pick-and-pack, and freight expenses.


Andrew Faris highlights the contribution margin targets DTC brands aim for. “I want to get at least above for most brands, the target would be at least above 60 points of margin after all of those costs; that is a DTC business that will hum,” he says. “If you can get above 65, you’re really good. If you can get above 70, you’re best in class.”


Audit your item pricing, fulfillment charges, and shipping fees together to verify that your[gross margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/gross-margin) remains above this 60% mark.


### Dilute fixed fulfillment charges with product bundles


Encouraging customers to purchase multiple items in a single transaction cuts your fulfillment costs per unit. On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/dossier-affordable-luxury-accessible-perfume-pricing) , Sergio Tache, founder of the fragrance brand[Dossier](https://dossier.co/) , says order bundling helped lower his business’s unit delivery expenses.


“We have a buy more, save more program where the more bottles you buy, the more you can save,” he says. “That helps people buy more perfume in one go. Which helps my[AOV](https://www.shopify.com/blog/average-order-value) , which helps my margins, because shipping more products in one order is actually cheaper on a per-unit basis.”


By increasing the units per order, the baseline package fee, box cost, and base shipping charge are distributed across multiple products, lowering the fulfillment expense for each item sold.


### Audit inventory holding times to avoid excess storage fees


Track how long each SKU stays in the warehouse to prevent old stock from running up monthly storage bills. Poor inventory management turns unsold inventory into a perpetual holding expense that eats away at product profits.


Calculate your[inventory turnover ratio](https://www.shopify.com/blog/inventory-turnover-ratio) and[days sales in inventory (DSI)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/days-sales-in-inventory) for each SKU monthly. If specific products sit in storage beyond 90 days without selling, implement automated markdown schedules, bundle slow sellers with popular items, or liquidate stagnant inventory to free up warehouse space and cash flow.


### Standardize and minimize package dimensions


Trim outer product packaging to keep package size as small as possible. Carriers bill lightweight parcels based on dimensional weight rather than scale weight whenever the volume of the box exceeds its physical mass.


Shaving even half an inch off an exterior box or switching from cartons to custom poly mailers can drop your package into a lower dimensional weight pricing tier, saving you money on carrier fees for every shipment sent. Run dimensional audits on your top 20% highest-volume SKUs to eliminate excess box volume and lower outgoing carrier charges on every order you process.


### Compare vetted logistics providers inside Shopify


Evaluating quotes across multiple fulfillment partners is difficult because every facility formats pricing differently, with varying receiving models, storage definitions, and pick-and-pack rates.


The[Shopify Fulfillment Network](https://www.shopify.com/fulfillment) recommendation tool lets you enter your fulfillment needs, sales locations, and package sizes to generate estimates from vetted 3PLs. This lets you compare rates without spending hours deciphering separate quote sheets. You can connect your store to these partners from your Shopify admin, and installing the app is free. You pay the 3PL only for the warehousing, fulfillment, and shipping services you use.


## 3PL pricing FAQ


### How do you calculate 3PL costs?


Add up all setup, inbound receiving, storage, pick-and-pack, packaging, shipping, returns, and account administration fees incurred during your billing cycle. Divide this total monthly expense by your monthly order count to find your landed fulfillment cost per order. This single-order baseline confirms whether your product pricing protects your target profit margins.


### What are the typical costs associated with logistics?


Logistics costs are divided into warehouse space, hands-on fulfillment labor, and parcel delivery. Storage encompasses bin or pallet fees alongside inbound receiving and inspection charges. Order processing and transportation cover item picking, packaging materials, carrier postage, and monthly account maintenance minimums.


### What are the disadvantages of using a 3PL provider?


Outsourcing fulfillment limits your direct daily control over custom packaging assembly and immediate quality inspections. Fixed monthly minimum spend requirements also present financial risk if your sales volume drops unexpectedly. Variable fuel surcharges, dimensional weight adjustments, and seasonal storage fees can make monthly logistics bills difficult to forecast.
